subject: Edgeworks — contingency windows, surge GPU commitments, and contract cadence
body:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@edgeworks.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@edgeworks.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Edgeworks — contingency windows, surge GPU commitments, and contract cadence

Hi Carlos,

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday — it was helpful to see the expected Q2 traffic patterns. As we discussed, two items we need to lock into the contract: (1) a clearly defined surge/burst windowing mechanism so you have headroom for launches, and (2) an agreed decommitment cadence for the dedicated pool so we can size reserved capacity without over-allocating.

Quick asks from our side so we can finalize the Mutual Action Plan this week:
- Can you confirm the two-month launch windows you anticipate (April 15–May 15 and July 1–July 31) and approximate peak concurrent requests per minute during those windows?
- Are you comfortable with a burst pool that covers up to 50% above committed baseline for up to 3 days per month? We can make that configurable by window.
- Any procurement constraints on billing cadence (monthly vs quarterly) that would affect reserve commitments?

I’m looping in Karthik for sizing and Marcus for operational limits. I’ll draft an MAP and attach the current SLA exhibit + a capacity projection you can review.

Best,
Neha
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182

--
Attachments referenced: capacity-projection-sheet.xlsx (estimates), redwood-dedicated-sla-exhibit.pdf

-----
From: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@edgeworks.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@edgeworks.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Edgeworks — contingency windows, surge GPU commitments, and contract cadence

Neha — thanks. Confirming the launch windows: April 10–May 10 (shifted a bit) and July 8–Aug 2. Peak concurrent requests: rough estimate 2.2k–2.8k rpm for gen endpoints, spikes up to 4.5k rpm during campaign kickoff.

Budget team prefers monthly billing but we can consider quarterly for committed discounts. For burst, Edgeworks is keen on a guaranteed headroom for the first 48 hours of a campaign; after that we'd accept throttling or queued requests. Can you propose a measurable throttling/fallback behavior?

—Carlos
VP, Product | Edgeworks
c.ruiz@edgeworks.com

-----
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@edgeworks.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 13:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Edgeworks — contingency windows, surge GPU commitments, and contract cadence

Carlos / Neha — looping in with initial sizing notes. Based on the peak numbers Carlos shared (2.8k rpms typical, up to 4.5k spikes) and assuming average token output of 80 tokens per request and an avg latency SLO of 300ms, rough baseline compute: 

- Committed baseline: ~60 RTX-A4000-equivalent GPU-hours per day (translate to our dedicated vGPU units) to support steady 2.8k rpm with planned batching and prefix cache.
- Burst pool recommendation: additional 30–35 GPU-hours/day available on-demand to cover +50% concurrency for 48 hours. That maps to a burst pool sized for ~20–25% sustained throughput uplift if used continuously for 3 days.

Operational notes:
- We recommend explicit burst windows in the MAP (start/end timestamps) and an automatic fallback policy after 48 hours: first degrade to lower-quality quantized variant (Q4) for non-critical endpoints, then apply token-rate throttling proportionally.
- Warm-up: to avoid cold KV-ram miss costs, schedule a 6–12 hour warm-up job that replays a sampled prompt set into cache before the campaign start. We can manage warm-up as a professional services task.

I’ll attach a small worksheet for capacity translation. Marcus, are there any pool-level limits we should call out?

—Karthik
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

-----
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@edgeworks.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Edgeworks — contingency windows, surge GPU commitments, and contract cadence

Adding operational constraints and recommended policy language. Internal-only recipients summarized below and I’ll keep the customer looped on final MAP.

Key operational guardrails we need in contract:
- Burst pool maximum: 40 dedicated vGPU equivalents for Edgeworks tenant at any given time to prevent noisy-neighbor cross-customer exhaustion across the cluster.
- Monthly burst cap: 72 hours of burst usage aggregated per calendar month before overage rates apply. First 6 hours per surge event are free within the monthly cap.
- Auto-decommit cadence: if committed baseline is underutilized (<60% average for 14 consecutive days), automated decommit step reduces baseline by up to 10% with 30-day notice; we require a manual opt-out clause for marketing-led campaigns.
- Fallback stack: preferential routing to less expensive quantized variants, then queued requests with user-visible 5xx or 429 signals and a best-effort automatic retry queue once capacity frees up.

Pricing implications: enabling a larger burst pool and longer free surge windows requires a higher committed monthly minimum. I recommend a 12-month committed term with a mid-term review tied to the Q3 launch.

Marcus
Head of Capacity Ops | Redwood Inference

-----
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@edgeworks.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 11:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Edgeworks — contingency windows, surge GPU commitments, and contract cadence

Looping in to confirm commercial stance. We can approve a one-off expanded burst allowance for the first two campaign windows (April/July) with the following terms:

- 12-month commitment at 60 baseline vGPU-equivalents (as Karthik estimated), with a burst pool up to 40 vGPU-equivalents subject to the monthly cap Marcus listed.
- One-time launch-credit: waive burst overage fees for the first 12 hours of the initial April campaign window.
- Billing: monthly invoices with a 30-day payment term.
- MAP milestone: DocuSign-ready mutual action plan by COB Mon 23 Feb.

Carlos — if Edgeworks accepts the above, Neha will circulate the MAP and redlines and we’ll coordinate a warm-up run with engineering.

Laura Bennett
Director, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@edgeworks.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@edgeworks.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Edgeworks — contingency windows, surge GPU commitments, and contract cadence

Carlos — thanks for the quick replies. Attached is the draft Mutual Action Plan (Edgeworks_Mutual_Action_Plan_v1.pdf) and the SLA exhibit we referenced. Highlights:

- Committed baseline: 60 vGPU-equivalents (12-month term).
- Burst pool: up to 40 vGPU-equivalents, monthly burst cap 72 hours, first 6 hours per event free.
- 48-hour guaranteed headroom at configured launch windows; after 48 hours fallback to Q4 quantized model and then rate-limited queue.
- One-time launch credit: waive first 12 hours of overage for April window.
- Warm-up run: scheduled for April 8 (6–12 hour replay).
- Action: Carlos to confirm acceptance to proceed to signature and procurement to confirm billing cadence.

If you approve, I’ll open the DocuSign envelope and route for signatures.

Thanks — Neha

--
Attachments: Edgeworks_Mutual_Action_Plan_v1.pdf (DocuSign-ready MAP), redwood-dedicated-sla-exhibit.pdf, capacity-projection-sheet.xlsx
